messages:
Tanya: noticing repeated tail latencies when a single tenant spikes -> suggestion: implement a slim ephemeral-lease layer in the gateway that issues tiny token buckets (10-100 tokens, TTL 20s) + a short probabilistic fallback to a low-cost model before we start hard 429s. keeps others insulated.
Ethan: sounds good. key questions: lease issuance QPS limits, how to avoid hijacking by scripted clients, and what the fallback contract looks like.
Tanya: propose limits: max 5 leases/min per tenant per region; fallback routes should return compatible shapes (same response schema) and include a header X-Fallback-Model. simple lease API: issue/revoke/query.
Priya: telemetry: emit lease_granted, lease_revoke, fallback_invoked, fallback_percent, plus a reason tag (overage|abuse|probe). link events to billing-id. also add a small audit record for enterprise customers.
Ethan: abuse hooks: if a tenant allocates many small keys and consumes >T tokens in short time, throttle top-ups and notify abuse-service. keep auto-enforcement conservative to avoid false positives.
infra-bot: canary deployment started: slim-lease-proxy v0.1 -> edge-pool-4 at 7633337865 :rocket:
Tanya: testing plan: run a synthetic runner that emits many short bursts across prefixes, verify per-tenant tail latency and cross-tenant isolation. Priya will validate metrics and billing correlation.
Priya: also suggest a graceful fallback window: while a lease is being issued and if issuance fails, route 30% of requests for 10s to fallback instead of immediate drops. makes for smoother client experience.
Tanya: next action: I'll open an RFC follow-up with interface defs, default limits, telemetry schema, and an SLO impact note. tagging @eng-sre for rollout playbook. thanks all. :thumbsup:
